mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5% is associated with a short-term decline in S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discount rates eroding future equity value.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant deviation from zero when FEDFUNDS > 5% for at least 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (PAYEMS) coincides with a sharp decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investor sentiment deteriorates and equity risk premia expand.
failure_condition: In regimes where PAYEMS > 8,000 for ≥10 consecutive months, 20-day forward returns remain positive with p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as expectations of future economic expansion boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 60-day forward returns show no out-of-sample predictability (Rank IC < 0.1) when HOUST growth exceeds +5% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and drives up S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses below 105 and remains below for ≥3 months
failure_condition: In supply contraction regimes, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO < 105 for ≥2 quarters.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of falling inflation (CPIAUCSL) while the Fed rate remains steady generate a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as expectations of looser policy and lower risk premia emerge.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses below 205 and remains below for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 20-day horizon, forward returns show no predictive power (Rank IC > 0.15) when CPIAUCSL declines for ≥4 months with FEDFUNDS unchanged.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (RSAFS) accompanied by a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a labor market tightening that increases risk and depresses S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% while RSAFS rises above 8 million in the same month
failure_condition: In tightening regimes, 60-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with the RSAFS-UNRATE interaction (Pearson ρ < -0.2, p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month accelerating trend in retail sales (PAYEMS) predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it indicates strengthening consumer confidence and upward earnings revisions.
failure_condition: Over 20-day horizon, returns are uncorrelated with PAYEMS trend (Spearman ρ < 0.1, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to supply-side constraints (e.g., persistent energy input costs) causes S&P 500 5-day forward returns to turn negative even when macroeconomic indicators are neutral.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth exceeds 4% for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: In supply-constrained regimes, 5-day forward returns are not negatively predicted by GDPC1 growth (p > 0.05).
